literal: Others' disgrace and their own disgrace, those who feel ashamed of - to modesty, dwelling place, will say the world.
translation: The world will call those who shrink from the disgrace of others as much as their own, the very abode of modesty.
modern: பிறருக்கு வரும் பழியையும் தமக்கு வரும் பழியையும் கண்டு வெட்கப்படுகின்றவர்களை, நாணம் தங்கியிருக்கும் உறைவிடம் என்று உலகம் சொல்லும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the highest standard of modesty or a sense of shame. It states that true modesty is not just avoiding one's own disgrace, but also feeling ashamed when others face disgrace. The word 'நாணுவார்' refers to those who instinctively shrink from any shameful act, regardless of who commits it. The world considers such empathetic and principled people to be the very dwelling place ('உறைபதி') of modesty itself.
